title: Dr. Phil blasts UFO 'lie': 'I don't trust the US government on this issue'
excerpt: Dr. Phil blasts UFO 'lie': 'I don't trust the US government on this issue'
content:
mystery

Express newspaper

04/09/2026 21:44

Dr. Phil McGraw has highlighted the large number of UFO reports that, according to him, the Pentagon has never investigated, despite the US government's extensive campaign to declassify documents related to these phenomena.

In a video released on Wednesday, Dr. Phil stated that he is "absolutely convinced" that the US government has been deceiving citizens for about 80 years, hiding information about unexplained UFO encounters and possible contact with extraterrestrial life.

Although he did not claim to possess evidence for the existence of extraterrestrial craft, the well-known television personality and author said that more than 1,800 serious UFO reports from citizens have been ignored by the Pentagon.

"Can some of them be explained? I'm sure they are, maybe all of them, I don't know. The thing is, no one in the government is looking into these cases," McGraw said.

He has previously criticized the way documents, photographs and videos allegedly related to government UFO files have been published.

According to McGraw, the entire transparency campaign is actually a huge hoax that continues to keep the public away from the truth about extraterrestrial life.

"Most of you are as angry as I am that the government has lied to our faces. What angers me most is that there is no government agency where ordinary American citizens can report UAPs," he said.

UAP is the term used today for "unidentified anomalous phenomena" and has largely replaced the traditional term UFO.

In February, President Donald Trump ordered the US Department of War to oversee the declassification and publication of all documents related to UFOs and extraterrestrial life.

So far, five sets of documents have been released, mainly from the FBI, CIA, NASA and the Pentagon.

However, most of them have contained vague reports, information not directly related to the case, or images too vague to be considered concrete evidence.

In the new video released on X, McGraw directly attacked the federal government, claiming that almost all private citizens in the US are left out of the process of reporting and discussing UAPs.

According to him, 93 percent of Americans have no official way to report a possible UFO sighting to the government or military.

This would include more than 310 million people.

Officially, the people who can directly submit a report to the federal government about unusual flying objects or other phenomena are current or former federal employees, members of the military, government contractors, and pilots.

"The government is turning a blind eye to most Americans. So if the government doesn't want to see this information, who is seeing it? Where is all this data ending up?" McGraw asked.

"If 99 percent of the cases turn out to be nothing unusual, fine. But what about the other one percent?"

According to Dr. Phil, ordinary citizens are left with only two private, non-governmental databases where anyone can report UFO sightings or other unexplained experiences.

They are the “National UFO Reporting Center”, NUFORC, and the “Mutual UFO Network”, MUFON.

McGraw noted that NUFORC currently has 1,855 reports classified as "Tier 1".

This category includes cases that the organization considers among the most difficult to explain and that, according to it, cannot be easily dismissed as birds, balloons, camera malfunctions, or man-made aircraft.

According to McGraw, although these cases have been independently analyzed and have been described as phenomena that may have unusual explanations, none of the 1,855 reports are likely to have been investigated by federal authorities.

This means that they are not included in the current process of declassifying and publishing UFO files.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon office that deals with the investigation of such phenomena, known as the "All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office", AARO, has repeatedly promised that in the future it will also accept reports from the general public.

However, this has not yet happened.

In a statement, AARO said: “Please note that reporting is currently limited to current or former U.S. government employees, military personnel, or contractors who have direct knowledge of U.S. government programs or activities related to UAPs dating back to 1945.”

“AARO currently DOES NOT accept reports of sightings or encounters with UAPs from the general public. In the future, the reporting opportunity will be expanded to the public and will include reports of any events related to UAPs.”

Republican Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna of Florida, who leads the House of Representatives caucus on declassifying federal secrets, has previously criticized AARO, accusing it of obstructing Congress' efforts to uncover more information on UFO cases.

She has accused the office of former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick of blocking and concealing information on UAPs from Congress and the public.

Kirkpatrick left AARO on December 1, 2023.

"They should say, 'Here's how you can submit your report through the appropriate channels.' But there is no right or wrong channel," McGraw said.

“Eighty years of telling us 'trust us' has gotten us nowhere.”

"I don't trust them at all on this issue," concluded Dr. Phil. /GazetaExpress/
